dialogues.scene: A groundhog looks up from a tiny clock, then at you.
lines: Oh, hello. Sorry, I was checking the time. It's mid-afternoon here. It's the middle of the night somewhere else.
I check a lot. It's a habit.

choices.label: Where's 'somewhere else'?
reaction: Oh, far. Past the river, over the mountains, in a whole other burrow.
I'm Biscuit, by the way. I know the exact distance, if you ever want it.

choices.label: That's a lot of clocks.
reaction: I have three on my wall.
One for here, one for there, and one for 'when we can talk.' The third is the most important.

choices.label: Nice to meet you, Biscuit.
reaction: Nice to meet you too. You have a kind face. I'm usually good at telling.
It's one of my small talents.

lines: I keep a little jar of notes.
Little things I want to tell someone, but can't yet. Like 'the sunset was orange today.'

choices.label: Who do you tell them to?
reaction: Someone who's far away. I save them up and read them out loud later.
It's slower than texting, but it feels like carrying water in cupped paws.

choices.label: Orange sunset? Tell me.
reaction: It was like someone spilled marmalade across the sky. I'd like someone to see it.
Now you have, in a way. Thank you.

choices.label: That's a lovely habit.
reaction: Thank you. It's a bit sentimental, I know.
But it makes the quiet hours feel less empty. Each note is a little lantern.

lines: My partner's name is Pip. He lives in the burrow over the mountain.
It's a six-hour time difference. When I wake up, he's about to sleep. We've learned to love the overlap.

choices.label: How long have you been apart?
reaction: Eight months. Two more to go before the next visit.
I've marked it on my wall with a very bright star.

choices.label: What's the overlap like?
reaction: Short, warm, a little sleepy. We have about an hour where both of us are awake.
I save my best stories for it. Pip saves his best yawns.

choices.label: Pip sounds special.
reaction: Pip's the kind of person who sends a goodnight message with a tiny drawing.
Every single day. I have eight months of drawings. They're all on my wall.

lines: Pip sent me a photo of his window today.
It was just the view. Nothing special. A tree and some fog. I stared at it for ten minutes.

choices.label: Why did it matter?
reaction: Because it was his morning. A small piece of his day I wasn't in.
And now I was, for a minute. It's like a postcard from a quiet world.

choices.label: That's sweet.
reaction: It's the little things that carry the weight. A window, a tree, a bit of fog.
I put the photo on my wall right next to the clocks.

choices.label: Did you send one back?
reaction: Yes. I sent my window.
Pip said 'your tree looks lonely.' I said 'it misses your tree.' We both got a bit teary at the same time.

lines: Okay, can I ask you something?
When you and your partner are apart, even for a day, how do you stay close? What works for you?
I'm collecting little ideas. I have a notebook for it.

choices.label: We send small messages throughout the day.
reaction: Small messages. Not big speeches. Just tiny pings. 'Thinking of you' in three words.
I could do that. Pip would love it.

choices.label: We have a shared playlist.
reaction: A playlist! That's lovely. Music is a good bridge. I'll make one with Pip.
We'll call it 'the overlap.' I already have a song in mind.

choices.label: Honestly, I miss them most at night.
reaction: Night's the hardest for me too. That's when the clocks get loud.
It helps to say it out loud to someone. Thank you for being honest.

lines: We tried to have a video call tonight.
The connection froze on Pip's face. Mid-laugh. Mouth open. I stared at it for a full minute.
Then I took a screenshot. It's my favorite photo now.

choices.label: That's adorable.
reaction: It's the best photo I own. Pip's mid-laugh, eyes squeezed, looking like a very happy fish.
I'd never trade it for a perfect one.

choices.label: A frozen face is hilarious.
reaction: It's SO silly!
I sent Pip the screenshot and he said 'delete that.' I said 'never.' We argued for an hour.
A very happy hour.

choices.label: Connection issues are the worst.
reaction: They are. But sometimes they give you a gift. A moment you didn't plan.
I'll take it. Pip's frozen laugh is my new favorite thing.

dialogues.scene: Biscuit sits quietly with the three clocks, none of them ticking loudly.
lines: Can I tell you something that isn't cheerful?
Sometimes I wonder if the distance is making us into letters instead of people.
What if we're better at missing each other than being together?

choices.label: That's a real fear.
reaction: It is. Thank you for not trying to fix it.
Sometimes I just need someone to say 'yeah, that's real.' I feel less alone already.

choices.label: You'll find out when you're together.
reaction: That's true. Distance can fool you both ways.
Maybe the only way to know is to stand in the same room. Two more months.

choices.label: Sit beside Biscuit.
reaction: ...Thank you. It's quiet, but it's nice. A different kind of company.
I'll tell Pip about this later. About the quiet.

lines: I told Pip about my worry. The letters one.
Pip said, 'I worry too. Every day.' He told me he's been practicing a surprise.
I wasn't supposed to say. Okay, I probably shouldn't have said that either.

choices.label: That's exciting.
reaction: I'm trying not to guess. Pip's good at surprises.
Last time it was a handmade puzzle of our favorite photo.
It took me a week to finish.

choices.label: Pip sounds thoughtful.
reaction: He really is. He doesn't say things loudly. He does them quietly, over time.
It's one of the reasons I love him.

choices.label: Your worry matters too.
reaction: Thank you. That means a lot. Saying it out loud helped.
The worry didn't vanish, but it's smaller. It fits in my pocket now.

lines: We counted down from ten together tonight.
Just 'ten, nine, eight...' Then we both said 'goodnight' at zero. It was so simple.
It felt like being in the same room. Like hearing someone breathe next to you.

choices.label: That sounds so intimate.
reaction: It was. A small ritual can carry a lot of love.
I think I'll do it every night. Even if one of us falls asleep before zero.

choices.label: Did you sleep well?
reaction: Better than I have in weeks. I dreamed about the border between two time zones.
A quiet line where both our clocks said midnight.

choices.label: Smile and listen.
reaction: Thank you for just listening. It's a bit like what Pip does.
No big words, just someone nearby. I think that's the best kind of company.

lines: Ten visits. I kept count. I'm a time-keeping sort of groundhog.
Pip's coming to visit next month. A whole week. I've been cleaning the burrow since sunrise.
I'm nervous and excited and I can't tell which is bigger.
And you? How are you and your partner? Honestly.

choices.label: We're good. Still learning.
reaction: Learning is good. That's the right word. Come by when Pip's here. I'll make something warm.
You'll love Pip. Everyone does.

choices.label: I miss them sometimes, even when we're close.
reaction: That's a real thing. Missing can happen in the same room. We talk about it.
It's okay. I'm glad you said it out loud.

choices.label: You make me want to say it more often.
reaction: That's the best thing anyone's said all week.
Okay, I'm going to add it to the jar of notes. It deserves its own lantern.

lines: Pip's changing jobs. Different shift. Now it's nights.
I'm trying to be cheerful about it. I'm reorganizing my clocks.

choices.label: That's a big shift.
reaction: It is! We'll need a new overlap. I've already started drawing a chart.
I'm calling it 'The Great Reshuffle.' Pip says it's too dramatic. It's perfect.

choices.label: How do you feel?
reaction: Honestly? A little wobbly. But also hopeful.
When something changes, you learn something new about how you love.

lines: I mailed Pip a box of fall leaves. It took four days.
I included a note: 'Open when the weather feels lonely.' He texted 'it's raining here, I'm opening it now.'

choices.label: Perfect timing.
reaction: It was! The mail knew. Pip sent a photo of the leaves on his desk.
I could almost smell the maple.
It felt like a hug that took four days to arrive.

choices.label: That's so thoughtful.
reaction: It's easy to be thoughtful when you miss someone. The hard part is waiting.
But waiting makes the box more precious.

lines: We watched the same movie at the same time, on different screens.
Pip kept pausing to say 'wait, this part!' I could hear him eating. It was almost like sitting together.

choices.label: That sounds cozy.
reaction: It really was. I made popcorn, and Pip made a bad copy of my popcorn.
We rated them. They lost. Gloriously.

choices.label: Did you laugh at the same parts?
reaction: Exactly the same parts. We both cried at the dog.
Pip said 'it's just a dog.' Then he said 'it's NOT just a dog.' A beautiful moment.

lines: There's a tiny storm on Pip's side. He said it's loud. I could hear it through the phone.
I stayed on the line until it passed. I didn't say anything. Just listened.

choices.label: That's love.
reaction: I think it is. Quiet presence. You don't have to fix the weather.
You just stay on the line while it happens. I'd do it forever.

choices.label: Did Pip feel better?
reaction: He said 'thanks for not hanging up.' It was the best thing I've heard in weeks.
I put it in the jar of notes.

lines: I woke up at 3 AM for a call and forgot why.
Then I saw Pip's face on the screen, half asleep, and remembered everything. I'd wake up for that any time.

choices.label: That sounds worth it.
reaction: It's the best kind of tired. The kind that's full instead of empty.
I fell asleep at 4 with the phone on my chest. Pip said I snored.
I did not.

choices.label: Do you get enough sleep?
reaction: Not really! But I'm learning to nap like a pro. A groundhog has to be flexible.
Two naps, a long yawn, and a lot of tea.

lines: I found a word in a book. 'Hiraeth.' It means missing a home you can't return to.
I told Pip. He said 'you're my home.' I had to sit down on the floor.

choices.label: That's beautiful.
reaction: I know. I stayed on the floor for ten minutes. The clocks kept ticking.
I'm not sure time was moving. I think it was just me and the word.

choices.label: You had to sit down?
reaction: My knees gave out! Emotionally. It's a real thing.
Pip laughed and said 'are you okay?' I said 'no, in the best way.'

lines: We're planning the visit. Pip's coming in thirty-one days. I made a countdown on the wall.
It's got stickers. I'm not ashamed.

choices.label: Stickers are essential.
reaction: Right? Each day I peel one off. It's a small ritual.
Like unwrapping a gift in tiny pieces. Day twelve has a tiny carrot on it.

choices.label: Thirty-one days? So close.
reaction: So close and so far. A month feels like both a blink and an ocean.
I'm trying to enjoy the middle part. The waiting part.

lines: Pip called me just to say 'I'm having a good day.'
No reason. No news. Just that. I think it was the best call we've had.

choices.label: That's so sweet.
reaction: It was! Not every call has to solve something.
Sometimes it's just a little 'I'm okay' sent across the miles.
I could feel it in my chest.

choices.label: A call for no reason?
reaction: The best kind. A reasonless call is love with its coat off.
We stayed on the line for an hour. We talked about socks.

lines: I still have the frozen-face screenshot. I made it my phone's lock screen.
Pip's mid-laugh, forever. I smile every time I check the time.

choices.label: That's adorable.
reaction: It is! And I check the time a lot, as you know.
So I smile a lot. It's a good trade.
Pip pretends to be annoyed but secretly loves it.

choices.label: Does Pip know?
reaction: He knows. He called it 'a crime.' Then he made one of me, caught mid-sneeze.
We're in an arms race of unflattering love.

lines: The jar of notes is full. I need a bigger jar.
I'm going to read them all to Pip when he visits. One a night. It'll take a month.

choices.label: Better get a big jar.
reaction: I found one at the market. It's shaped like a pear. Pip will love it.
Or find it ridiculous. Both are good outcomes.

choices.label: That sounds romantic.
reaction: I hope so. Some notes are silly, some are sad.
But all of them say 'I thought of you.' That's the whole point.

lines: Remember the three clocks? I got a fourth.
It's set to Pip's time, but it runs backwards. It's a joke. I don't know why I bought it.

choices.label: A backwards clock?
reaction: It runs the wrong way. Pip says it fits.
'We're a little backwards sometimes, but we get there.' I put it by the door.

choices.label: Four clocks is a lot.
reaction: It is! The walls are getting crowded. But each clock holds a different kind of waiting.
I'm running out of wall, not out of love.

lines: The ten-count at bedtime. We still do it, every night.
Even when we're tired. Even when we're cranky. 'Ten, nine, eight...' It's the most reliable thing in my life.

choices.label: That's lovely.
reaction: I think so too. Some nights we say it in whispers.
Some nights we say it laughing. The number's always the same, but the feeling changes.

choices.label: Even on grumpy nights?
reaction: Especially on grumpy nights. It's hard to stay mad when you're counting down together.
By 'three,' someone's already giggling.

lines: Hot take: Distance doesn't test love. It just shows you how much you've learned to pay attention.

choices.label: That's a good way to put it.
reaction: Thanks. I think distance makes you listen harder.
When all you have is a voice, you hear everything in it. Every pause, every breath.

choices.label: It tests it a bit.
reaction: Fair. It does. Some days it tests me a lot.
But I think attention is the thing that holds. Attention and a good clock.

lines: Hot take: A good goodnight is better than a grand gesture.

choices.label: I'd agree.
reaction: It's the daily proof. A grand gesture is a firework.
A good goodnight is a lantern that stays lit.
I need both, but I need the lantern more.

choices.label: Grand gestures are fun too.
reaction: They are! I'll take a bouquet any day.
But I'd still choose a soft 'goodnight' on a rainy Tuesday. That's where the love lives.

lines: Hot take: Time zones are just love's way of making you value the overlap.

choices.label: That's lovely.
reaction: I made that up during a very sleepy afternoon. It stuck.
The overlap is where we shine. It's short, so we don't waste it.

choices.label: Love's love, overlap or not.
reaction: True. Love's love. But overlap is the cozy bit.
If I could bottle one hour, it would be the one where we're both awake and a little silly.

lines: I'm trying to learn something new. How do you comfort your partner when they're having a hard day?
Not fix. Comfort.

choices.label: I just sit with them.
reaction: Sitting with them. I'm learning that.
Pip's far, so I have to do it through a screen.
I stay on the line and don't talk. It works better than I expected.

choices.label: I bring them something small.
reaction: A small thing. Tea, a snack, a blanket. I wish I could do that.
Maybe I'll mail a tea bag next. A tiny comfort in an envelope.

lines: Do you and your partner ever run out of things to say?
Pip and I have days where we just sit on a call in silence.

choices.label: Yeah, and it's nice.
reaction: It is. Silence is a good sign, I think.
When you can be quiet together, you've built a home inside the call.

choices.label: Not really, we talk a lot.
reaction: That's lovely. Chatty love is warm. We're the quiet kind, mostly.
But I'm glad both kinds exist. They all count.

lines: What's a small thing your partner does that makes you feel seen?
I keep a list. It helps on lonely days.

choices.label: They remember what I like.
reaction: Remembering. That's a big one. Pip remembers I like pears.
Every time he sees a pear, he sends a picture.
I've got a whole album of pears.

choices.label: They notice when I'm off.
reaction: Noticing is magic. Pip can tell from the tone of my 'hello.' Distance hasn't dulled it.
If anything, it's sharper.

dialogues.scene: Biscuit hands you a small envelope with a faint smile.
lines: This is for you. A note from the jar. One of the good ones.
It says: 'Somebody out there is glad you exist.' I thought you might need it today.

choices.label: Open the note.
reaction: I wrote it a while ago for no one in particular.
Today it felt like it was for you. That's what notes do.
They wait for the right person.

choices.label: Thank you, Biscuit.
reaction: You're very welcome. It's just a small thing. But small things are the ones that stay.
Keep it somewhere you'll find it by accident.

dialogues.scene: Biscuit leads you to a hilltop. The sky is turning orange.
lines: This is where I come to feel closer to Pip.
If I look in that direction, past the mountain, I like to imagine he's looking back.

choices.label: I bet they are.
reaction: I bet so too. The sky is the same sky, just wearing a different hour.
Sunset here is almost lunch there. Funny, isn't it?

choices.label: Sit and watch the sunset.
reaction: Thank you for sitting with me. It's nicer with company.
I think Pip would have liked you. He will like you. I'll make sure of it.
